statements.quote: The basic science, however, suggests that, if these results are replicated, there’s yet more data for the profound biology underlying the relationship between our microbiome, our mental health, and our environment, in determining who gets sick, when, and with what.
statements.context: Closing reflection on the Yolken et al. 2019 PLOS ONE cohort study that linked early household cat exposure to about double the odds of schizophrenia and found dogs protective (mechanism: Toxoplasma gondii and microbial co-travelers). The author conditions on future replication of the results; the consequent is an interpretive claim that replication would add evidence for microbiome-mental-health biology, not a dated world-state call.
statements.note: Borderline: conditional on replication (a future event), but the consequent is interpretive rather than a specific forecast. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: NY, CA, IL, and more coming soon, and enrolling for research like SAINT OLO globally.
statements.context: Footnote 1 attached to the author's line that he practices at Fermata in NYC and Acacia Clinics in Sunnyvale, CA, still sees patients, and readers can book a consultation. The footnote says the practice covers NY, CA and IL with more states coming soon, and is enrolling for research such as SAINT OLO globally.
statements.note: Own-organization expansion claim (Fermata / Acacia Clinics); coder marks CONTROL. Low forecast value.

statements.quote: The FDA review of this non-label makes it clear—people are going to prescribe this anyway. Nothing we say about this negative trial will stop them.
statements.context: Section 'Irritability Associated with Autism…Problematic Data' of Abilify I. Otsuka's maintenance trial of aripiprazole for irritability in autistic children was negative (p=0.097) and the FDA declined a maintenance label. The author quotes the FDA reviewer ('It is unlikely that the results ... would significantly alter the clinical practice of prescribers ... it is likely that aripiprazole would be continued') and adopts the view that prescribers will keep using it regardless.
statements.note: Endorsed restatement of the FDA reviewer's forecast that prescribers would continue aripiprazole despite the negative maintenance trial; the author's stance is the statement.

statements.quote: For now, fish oil probably helps reduce the risk of conversion to psychosis in high risk individuals.
statements.context: 'The bottom line' of the article after reviewing Amminger's Vienna omega-3 RCT (2010) and its 6.7-year follow-up (2015), the Montazer 2022 meta-analysis (no PANSS benefit, some GAF benefit), the ALSPAC cohort data, and the Chen et al. 2024 network meta-analysis (lower transition odds at 6, 12 and 24+ months). The author's provisional verdict on omega-3 supplementation for individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis.
statements.note: Borderline: an evidential verdict on present efficacy rather than a call about a future state; 'For now' marks it as provisional. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: What I have not addressed is the lack of efficacy in bipolar depression . We will save that for tomorrow.
statements.context: Closing of Abilify II (mania): the author has not addressed aripiprazole's lack of efficacy in bipolar depression and says the next article, tomorrow, will cover it. He then hedges: 'That will be tomorrow…probably!'
statements.note: Own-newsletter publishing plan; coder marks CONTROL. Hedged two lines later with 'probably'.

statements.quote: I have learned that when there is a best-selling drug, there is a federal case brought for illegal marketing. These cases are routinely settled by the DOJ for way, way less money than the drug made thanks to said illegal marketing.
statements.context: 'The Federal Settlements' section of Abilify V. The author, as a self-described dilettante historian of pharmaceuticals, states a general pattern: every best-selling drug attracts a federal illegal-marketing case, and the DOJ routinely settles for far less than the drug earned; he adds that this may be a rational strategy for the companies. Illustrated by the 2007 $515m BMS settlement and the 2008 $4m Otsuka settlement over Abilify.
statements.note: Borderline: a general regularity inferred from history, stated in generic present tense; not an explicit dated forecast. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: there is just SO MUCH that I will require another article to even get to state-level or private class action lawsuits about abilify. And those? I promise, they are much more exciting than these federal cases.
statements.context: Near the end of Abilify V: the author says the litigation topic needs another article covering state-level and private class-action lawsuits, and promises those will be more exciting than the federal cases. He adds that he hopes readers will 'compulsively read the next article in this series', foreshadowing the compulsive-behavior lawsuits article.
statements.note: Own-newsletter publishing plan; coder marks CONTROL.

statements.quote: And now, in what may or may not be the final installment depending on how I feel, is the final article of this week on the topic.
statements.context: Opening of Abilify V (2024-03-22): the author says this is the final Abilify article of the week and may or may not be the final installment of the series. Later in the same post he says another article on state and class-action suits is needed.
statements.note: Own-newsletter plan; coder marks CONTROL. Hedged.
